normalization.caption: Fig. 12 | Paired environments at comparable intensity and their relation to lifecycle timing. a, Pre- and post-peak RH in 8,966 shared 10 kt intensity-bin pairs from 2,327 cyclones. b, The same observed RH differences plotted against signed duration asymmetry A. Hexagons count cyclone–intensity-bin pairs; the dashed lines indicate equal RH and zero difference. These descriptive panels contain no fitted trend. c, Raw, screened and adjusted post-minus-pre estimates for five environments, with each cyclone given unit total weight across its valid bins. d, Background-adjusted slopes per 0.1 A. Cells give one estimate in the stated native unit; colour identifies interval direction, not magnitude. Full intervals and cyclone/pair counts are in Table S4c,d,e,i,k. Raw contrasts and slopes against A retain separate five-test Benjamini–Hochberg families. Raw, screened and slope intervals use 2,000 SID resamples; adjusted ranges are conditional 2.5th–97.5th percentiles of successful support-screened refits. PI adjustment is unestimated because joint support is absent; its screened mean and A slope retain their own samples. RH is the 700/500 hPa mean, advection is storm-relative horizontal humidity advection, and PI − V is potential intensity minus concurrent maximum sustained wind. A compares time to first LMI with time after last LMI, excluding their intervening span. Exact-wind comparisons are in Table S4h1,h2,h3.
